name: Reverse Barbell Curl
description: The reverse barbell curl is performed with a straight bar using an overhand (pronated) grip. It targets the brachioradialis, brachialis, and extensor muscles of the forearm. Because the biceps brachii is in a mechanically disadvantaged position when pronated, the forearm extensors and brachioradialis must work harder. This exercise builds forearm thickness and complements standard underhand curls for complete elbow flexor development.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a barbell with a pronated grip, shoulder-width. Arms extended at the thighs.
execution.setup_instructions: Use lighter weight than underhand curls. The pronated position reduces overall lifting capacity.
steps: Step 1: Curl the barbell upward with the overhand grip, keeping elbows at the sides.
Step 2: Curl to maximum elbow flexion, maintaining pronation throughout.
Step 3: Lower slowly back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Wrists breaking into flexion or extension
safety_considerations: Straight bar may cause wrist discomfort — use an EZ-bar if needed
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension to full elbow flexion.
